_note: Pencil, unreviewed. Each claim is built by code from ONE row of outcomes_sample.csv (or the other_tables files). The model may only choose which claim ids to show and may not alter slot values. 'check' is what the verifier runs on the final sentence.
_global_gate: A claim is eligible only if its row has no sanity_flags entry that mentions its section (C1_REJECTED, C7_REJECTED, C21_REJECTED, C11_bands_sum_*, C11_blank) and every needed field is non-empty. Otherwise the tool prints 'not reported / could not verify' for that field.

claims.check: Every integer in the sentence equals a slot value; rate_pct recomputed by code; admitted_total <= applied_total; row flag C1_REJECTED absent.
claims.example: In 2025-26, Georgia Tech admitted 8,921 of 66,881 first-year applicants (13.3%).

claims.template: {school_name} ({cds_year}) admitted {admitted_men:,} of {applied_men:,} men and {admitted_women:,} of {applied_women:,} women who applied.
claims.check: Four integers match slots; men+women within 10% of applied_total (flag C1_sex_rows_do_not_sum_to_total blocks it). Context only: never use sex as an input to a label.
claims.example: University of Michigan (2025-26) admitted 7,593 of 53,044 men and 10,322 of 56,068 women who applied.

claims.template: {school_name} ({cds_year}) admitted {in_state_admitted:,} of {in_state_applied:,} in-state, {out_of_state_admitted:,} of {out_of_state_applied:,} out-of-state and {nonresident_admitted:,} of {nonresident_applied:,} international applicants.
claims.check: Six integers match; present for 14 of 24 sample colleges only; if blank say 'residency split not reported'.
claims.example: Georgia Tech (2025-26) admitted 3,691 of 12,527 in-state, 4,513 of 44,596 out-of-state and 716 of 9,758 international applicants.

claims.template: {school_name} ({cds_year}) rates {factor_label} as '{c7_value}' in its own Common Data Set (section C7).
claims.check: c7_value is one of the four allowed strings and equals the row value; row has >=15 of 18 factors readable (else C7_REJECTED). Never add 'so it matters X much': C7 is a self-description, not a weight.
claims.example: UCLA (2025-26) rates the application essay 'Very Important' and standardized test scores 'Not Considered' in its own Common Data Set (section C7).

claims.template: Among {school_name} enrolled first-years who submitted SAT scores ({sat_submit_pct}% of them did), the middle 50% scored {sat_p25}-{sat_p75} ({cds_year}).
claims.check: Numbers match; the clause about the submit share is mandatory (a missing clause fails the check); no phrase implying 'admitted students'.
claims.example: Among Georgia Tech enrolled first-years who submitted SAT scores (78% of them did), the middle 50% scored 1370-1530 (2025-26).

claims.template: {gpa_400}% of {school_name} enrolled first-years had a GPA of 4.0 and {gpa_375_399}% were between 3.75 and 3.99 ({cds_year}; average {avg_gpa}; {gpa_submitted_pct}% of students supplied a GPA).
claims.check: Bands sum to 98-102 (else C11_bands_sum flag blocks it); the word 'enrolled' and the submit share must appear; GPA scale is the school's own (some report weighted GPAs above 4.0).
claims.example: 38.8% of University of Michigan enrolled first-years had a GPA of 4.0 and 55.1% were between 3.75 and 3.99 (2025-26; average 3.9; 97.8% of students supplied a GPA).

claims.template: {school_name} ({cds_year}) reports {ed_admitted:,} admitted of {ed_applied:,} early decision applicants.
claims.check: ed_admitted <= ed_applied, ed_applied >= 100, ed_admitted < admitted_total (else C21_REJECTED). Valid for only 2 of 24 sample colleges. Never say ED is 'easier'.
claims.example: Boston University (2025-26) reports 2,165 admitted of 6,907 early decision applicants.

claims.template: {school_name} ({cds_year}) offered {wl_offered:,} students a wait-list place; {wl_accepted:,} accepted and {wl_admitted:,} were later admitted.
claims.check: wl_admitted <= wl_accepted <= wl_offered; three integers match.
claims.example: Yale (2025-26) offered 944 students a wait-list place; 738 accepted and 32 were later admitted.

claims.template: UC reports {campus} admitted {admits:,} of {applicants:,} fall 2026 first-year applicants; the middle 50% of admitted students had a UC-calculated GPA of {admitted_gpa_p25}-{admitted_gpa_p75}.
claims.check: Numbers match the CSV row; the GPA clause says 'admitted' (this is an admitted-student range, not an admit rate by GPA). UC GPA is weighted and capped.
claims.example: UC reports UCLA admitted 15,903 of 146,692 fall 2026 first-year applicants; the middle 50% of admitted students had a UC-calculated GPA of 4.20-4.30.

claims.template: Texas reports {institution} accepted {tx_accepted:,} of {tx_applied:,} Texas first-time applicants in fall 2025; {accepted_top10:,} of those accepted were in the top 10% of their class.
claims.check: Numbers match; no sentence may divide top-10 admits by anything but accepted (there is no 'applied by rank' column, so no admit rate by rank).
claims.example: Texas reports The University of Texas at Austin accepted 15,931 of 37,691 Texas first-time applicants in fall 2025; 12,331 of those accepted were in the top 10% of their class.

claims.template: Your SAT of {student_sat} is {below|inside|above} the {school_name} middle-50% range of {sat_p25}-{sat_p75} for enrolled students who submitted.
claims.check: The comparison word is recomputed by code from the three numbers. Arithmetic only.
claims.example: Your SAT of 1400 is inside the Georgia Tech middle-50% range of 1370-1530 for enrolled students who submitted.

claims.source: data/reddit_collegeresults_shreybirmiwal (team data; counts not re-verified in this report)
claims.template: Among {n_similar} self-reported posters with a similar profile who applied to {college}, {k_admitted} reported an acceptance. This sample is self-selected and does not represent all applicants.
claims.check: n_similar >= 15 (else 'too few to say'); stamp text mandatory; never sets the label.
claims.example: (Counts not verified by this report; the team computes them from its own file.)

cannot_support: Any probability, chance, odds or percentage for one student.
Admit rate by GPA band or by test band for a college: CDS C9/C11 are shares of ENROLLED students; UC and Texas give admitted-student ranges or admits by rank group, not rates by band.
Any statement of how much a C7 factor 'counts' or that an essay or activity raised or lowered a decision.
That early decision or early action raises a student's chance (C21 counts are usable for 2 of 24 sample colleges; C22 has no counts at all).
Test-score position for a college whose percentiles are blank or whose submit share is low, without the submit-share clause.
Anything about a college whose row is flagged REJECTED for that section.
